Additional Advocate General

 Special Government Pleader
 Order

This Writ Petition has been filed in the nature of Mandamus, seeking a direction to the second respondent/Special Revenue Divisional Officer / Land Acquisition Officer, Land Acquisition and Management Office, Madurai, to pay compensation for acquisition of the lands of the petitioner in survey No. 769/1C, totally measuring 2560 sq.ft in Balakrishnapuram Village, Dindigul East Taluk,
Dindigul District.
2.The petitioner had filed L.A.O.P.No.44 of 2023 before the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Principal District Court, Dindigul questioning the very same award.

The land had been acquired,
compensation had been determined and award was also passed.
Questioning the Award in the manner known to law, the petitioner had filed land acquisition proceedings and it is pending.
The petitioner had also taken necessary steps in accordance with law.
In that land proceedings, not only the petitioner herein, but also 15 other land owners are arrayed as petitioners.
They are all joined together and filed the aforementioned L.A.O.P.No.44 of 2023.
3.It is contended by the learned Additional Advocate General that the petitioner has not handed over the possession and is obstructing acquisition of land.
4.The learned counsel for the petitioner stated that he is having two minor children, who require assistance owing to mental illness.
The respondents may consider that particular aspect.

However,
the petitioner cannot stall the proceedings on that ground.
The petitioner had already initiated necessary procedure for that purpose.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
5.Once compensation is fixed, award is passed, then the possession of land has to be handed over by the petitioner.
The respondents are not the authorities to consider.
So far as the children of the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner may seek relief independently before the appropriate authority, but not with the present respondents.

sentences.text: Before the Collector's Office, the petitioner tried to commit self-immolation.
The concerned Advocate is responsible for the conduct of the petitioner.
7.It is made clear that any Advocate, who files vakalat for the client has not only to advise the client with the legal steps to be taken, but also prevent them from committing unlawful acts.
Threat to self-immolation is an unlawful act.

8.The petitioner is directed to voluntarily hand over the land within a period of two weeks, from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, or else, the respondents may take necessary steps for possession of land in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis manner known to law.
The acquisition is for public welfare and social interest.
The petitioner must realise that he is also part of society and not living a solitary life.
9.I am confident that the learned Principal District Judge, Dindigul would pass appropriate orders on considering all materials available on record.
10.For the above reasons, this Writ Petition stands dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
